title: Auto-Renew Loyalty Credit for Restored Domain Registrations
content:
## Desk ruling — auto-renew loyalty credit on redemption restores

Ruling for Domain Registrations: on a redemption restore billed on or after 1 December 2025, the restored-year autopay credit, one of the restored-year credits, is USD 0.50 for each restored year where the domain's auto-renew setting is on and no declined auto-renew attempt is recorded on it less than 12 whole months before the day of the restore, USD 0.20 for each restored year where the setting is on and at least one such declined attempt is recorded, and nothing where auto-renew is off.

**Input — judgement — result**

| Auto-renew setting on the domain | Declined auto-renew attempts recorded on the domain in the last 12 whole months before the restore day | Credit per restored year |
|---|---|---|
| On | None | USD 0.50 |
| On | One or more | USD 0.20 |
| Off | Any number | Nothing |

Notes on the ruling:
- The setting read is the one the domain carries on the day of the restore.
- Only declined attempts recorded on this domain count; a decline is inside the look-back while fewer than 12 whole months separate it from the restore day, a month counting once its day of the month is reached. A decline recorded on 6 February 2028 still counts for a restore on 5 February 2029 and no longer counts for a restore on 6 February 2029.
- With the setting off, no decline history changes the result.

*Hypothetical case:* auto-renew on, one declined attempt recorded eight months before the restore, one restored year: USD 0.20.
